2.2 Lithology, TOC and Rock-Eva! 2.2.1 Source Rock Potential and Kerogen Type Twenty-five samples from the Hordaland Group ( m) were described (seventeen side-wall cores and eight cuttings samples). The section consist

e and one coal cuttings sample. The latter is strongly suspected of being lignite additive. All the sandstone and siltstone samples have very low to fairly low TOC contents (0.01 % to %). The claystone sample has good TOC content (1.61 %). It has hydrogen index of 249 mg HC/g TOC and an oxygen index of 41 mg 002/g TOC, indicating kerogen type II/III. It has

earing zone, except for the 1927 sample which is outside this zone. Most of the samples are probably from an oil zone, judged from the very high HC values. The TOC normalised values are high for all these sandstone samples. No samples from the Middle Heather Formation (1964 - m) were extracted, as the previous analyses have demonstrated the low contents of i

al of significance. Occasional samples have fair potential for gas generation but are very immature. Sidewall core samples from the Draupne Formation have rich TOC content and an oxygen index indicative of type II kerogen. The petroleum potential is good (14.9 HC/g TOC) and the Draupne Formation is thought to have good potential for generation of oil, but it

ples are largely reworked. These samples suggest the lower levels of the Lower Heather Formation shales to have fair to excellent potential for oil generation. TOC contents also vary widely however (also true for the upper levels) which suggests rapid vertical variations in the amount and quality of the organic matter input.
